concerns: The manuscript is a demonstration proposal with no empirical evaluation, comparative benchmarks, or quantitative measurements of accuracy, latency, cost, or optimization effectiveness.
Technical details of the query optimizer, cost-latency modeling, and LLM-driven plan selection are only summarized at a high level without validation.
The authors explicitly state that Carnot provides no guarantees on plan accuracy or correctness, leaving the core system claims unverified.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the system concept is interesting and clearly described as a demonstration track paper, the absence of systematic experimental evaluations, comparative benchmarks, and detailed technical validation creates significant scientific uncertainty regarding its performance and optimization effectiveness.

evidence.excerpt:
Enterprises increasingly seek to query data lakes using natural
language via AI-driven tools like semantic operators or deep re-
search agents. However, the latter operates as an opaque black
box, hiding its intermediate reasoning and data retrieval steps, and
failing to expose controls for managing API costs and execution
latency. Meanwhile, the former can be prohibitively expensive for
enterprise-scale data lakes. Consequently, analysts using these sys-
tems lack the agency to intercept hallucinated premises, verify
intermediate results, or correct the system's trajectory. We present
Carnot, an interactive execution engine for AI-driven analytics.
Carnotcompiles natural language requests into physical execu-
tion graphs and surfaces them through an interactive notebook
interface. Rather than waiting blindly for a final output, users can

evidence.excerpt:
human in the loop at every step.
Our demo showcasesCarnot's interactive planning and execu-
tion over datasets from academic benchmarks [3] and enterprise
workloads motivated by industry partners. To see transparent exe-
cution in action, attendees will issue queries and inspect the result-
ing DAGs before any computation begins; they may drill into any
operator to view its generated code, prompt, or a natural language
summary of its intent. To experience steerability, attendees will
execute a query step-by-step, intercept a faulty intermediate result,
and edit the corresponding notebook cell;Carnotwill then resume
execution from the corrected point without re-running upstream
operators. Finally, to highlightCarnot's cost-aware optimization,
attendees will configure explicit cost and latency constraints in the
interface;Carnotwill show how the planner dynamically swaps
operator

expensive LLM operators, the planner first
invokes adata discoverysubagent that samples the dataset, per-
forms schema analysis, and summarizes dataset structure. The
QueryOptimizer follows, inspired by the Cascades-style optimizer
of Abacus [8]. It shares a similar set of implementation and transfor-
mation rules, but differs in its use of an LLM agent to select the final
physical plan from the estimated Pareto frontier of cost, latency,
and quality. The library also contains a streaming and notebook
execution layer, a storage engine with caching support, and an
index catalog for managing semantic indices.

evidence.excerpt:
Carnotdoes not provide guarantees on plan accuracy or correct-
ness. We could modify the optimizer to provide statistical guaran-
tees with respect to an oracle [6], but this is a soft guarantee since
the oracle can also be wrong. Alternatively, better interfaces may
improve users' ability to verify plan correctness. In the future, we
also plan to extendCarnotto support search over the web (akin to
traditional Deep Research) and general tool calling. We also aim to
explore improvements to the notebook interface which can better
highlight the non-linear nature of most plan DAGs.

blocking_reasons: The manuscript is a demonstration proposal with no empirical evaluation, comparative benchmarks, or quantitative measurements of accuracy, latency, cost, or optimization effectiveness.
Technical details of the query optimizer, cost-latency modeling, and LLM-driven plan selection are only summarized at a high level without validation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No formal quantitative evaluation or comparative benchmark metrics are reported in this demo track paper.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Qualitative demonstration walkthrough scenarios with sample dataset queries.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: An LLM agent selects the final physical plan from an estimated Pareto frontier of cost, latency, and quality.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding interactive plan inspection, steering, and partial re-execution are illustrated through scenario walkthroughs and UI figures, but no empirical quantitative evidence or comparative experimental data are provided to substantiate general system claims.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The paper is a four-page demonstration proposal describing three planned interactive user scenarios rather than a controlled empirical evaluation or benchmark assessment of system performance, accuracy, latency, or cost trade-offs.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No formal quantitative evaluation or comparative benchmark metrics are reported in this demo track paper.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Qualitative demonstration walkthrough scenarios with sample dataset queries.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: An LLM agent selects the final physical plan from an estimated Pareto frontier of cost, latency, and quality.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that Carnot offers no statistical guarantees on plan accuracy or correctness and currently lacks web search and general tool-calling capabilities.
primary.method_assessment: The system architecture connects a chat frontend, notebook interface, and backend query planner and optimizer based on Cascades-style rules, but technical details on cost-latency modeling, plan pruning, and LLM-driven adaptation are only summarized at a high level for a demo presentation.
primary.quality_rationale: While the system concept is interesting and clearly described as a demonstration track paper, the absence of systematic experimental evaluations, comparative benchmarks, and detailed technical validation creates significant scientific uncertainty regarding its performance and optimization effectiveness.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents Carnot, an interactive execution engine that compiles natural language deep research queries into physical Directed Acyclic Graphs presented via chat and notebook interfaces for inspection, steering, and re-execution.

scholarly_quality.rationale: While the system concept is interesting and clearly described as a demonstration track paper, the absence of systematic experimental evaluations, comparative benchmarks, and detailed technical validation creates significant scientific uncertainty regarding its performance and optimization effectiveness.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly note that Carnot offers no statistical guarantees on plan accuracy or correctness and currently lacks web search and general tool-calling capabilities.
